Covariance
Covariance tells us the direction of the relationship
between two variables.
If 𝑋increases:
• If 𝑌generally increases → positive covariance
• If 𝑌generally decreases → negative covariance
• If there is no consistent linear movement → covariance is 
close to 0

For sample data:
Cov 𝑋 𝑌 =

• 𝑋, 𝑌= observations 
• 𝑋ത, 𝑌ത= sample means 
• 𝑛= number of observations

Correlation
7
Correlation measures both the direction and strength 
of the linear relationship between two variables.
The correlation coefficient is represented by:
𝑟
Its value always lies between:
−1≤r≤+1​
Correlation 𝐫 Interpretation
+1 Perfect positive correlation
Close to +1 Strong positive relationship
0 No linear correlation
Close to −1 Strong negative relationship
−1 Perfect negative correlation
